title: Reset an enterprise account password
symptoms: A user cannot sign in because a password is forgotten, expired, or rejected.
steps: Verify the caller with the approved identity check.
Confirm the account is active and not under a security hold.
Issue a one-time password reset link.
Ask the user to set a new password and verify sign-in.
resolution: Password reset completed and sign-in confirmed.

title: Unlock a locked enterprise account
symptoms: A user receives an account locked or too many attempts message.
steps: Verify the caller's identity.
Check the directory lock state and recent failed attempts.
Unlock the account if no security hold is present.
Have the user retry and confirm successful sign-in.
resolution: Account unlocked after verification and access restored.

title: Diagnose remote access connection failures
symptoms: A remote worker cannot establish a secure connection or the connection drops.
steps: Capture the exact error, device, network, and client version.
Check service status and the user's entitlement.
Verify device time, certificate validity, and multi-factor authentication.
Collect client diagnostics and escalate if the failure persists.
resolution: Remote access restored or diagnostic evidence attached for network escalation.

title: Triage an enterprise application outage
symptoms: Multiple users cannot open or use a business-critical application.
steps: Confirm scope, affected locations, start time, and business impact.
Check service health and recent releases.
Link the ticket to an active incident if one exists.
Escalate with evidence and impact.
resolution: Incident linked or application team engaged with scope and impact documented.

title: Troubleshooting Monitor Power and Blank Display
symptoms: The monitor screen is completely blank, does not display any video output, and appears powered off.
steps: Verify that the monitor power cable is securely connected to both the monitor and an active power outlet.
Locate the control buttons on the underside or bezel of the monitor, specifically checking the far right side.
Press the rightmost power button to power on the unit.
Check if the power indicator light turns on and video appears on the screen.
If the screen still does not turn on after pressing the button, verify the display cable connection or escalate the ticket to Desktop Services for hardware inspection.
resolution: The monitor powers on and normal display function is restored by pressing the physical power button located on the bottom right of the monitor.

title: Connecting a Workstation to a Network Printer Using MyPrint App
symptoms: User cannot connect their workstation or laptop to an office network printer.
steps: Open the MyPrint (or My Print Services) application on the workstation.
Select the option to connect to a printer.
Locate and select the desired printer from the available printer list.
Confirm the connection establishes successfully.
If the printer does not appear or fails to connect, verify network connectivity and printer IP reachability, then escalate to Tier 2 support if necessary.
resolution: The workstation successfully connects to the selected printer through the MyPrint application.

title: Unlocking Active Directory Account After Failed Self-Service Password Reset
symptoms: User reports being unable to reset their Active Directory password and is unable to log in due to an account block or lockout status.
steps: Verify caller identity using standard security verification questions.
Open identity management console (such as SailPoint) or Active Directory management tools to inspect the target user account.
Review account status to confirm if the account is flagged as blocked or locked out.
Execute the unlock or unblock action on the user account in the identity management tool.
Prompt the user to attempt authentication or initiate the password reset process again to confirm resolution.
If the account remains locked or authentication fails after unblocking, escalate the incident to Tier 2 Identity and Access Management.
resolution: The user account is unlocked in the identity management system, enabling the user to authenticate successfully.

title: Troubleshooting Laptop Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) Associated with Vendor Security Software
symptoms: User laptop encounters a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) preventing normal system boot and workstation use, reportedly linked to third-party endpoint protection software (e.g., CrowdStrike).
steps: Identify and document the exact BSOD error code and failing driver or system file if visible on screen.
Check internal IT bulletins and vendor status pages for known issues, outages, or pending agent/BIOS updates.
Confirm whether the issue is isolated to a specific machine or part of a wider third-party vendor incident.
Communicate vendor status and expected recovery timelines to the user if a vendor-side patch is required.
Escalate unresolved or critical devices to Endpoint Engineering if official safe mode workarounds or recovery media become available.
resolution: No local fix was verified in the incident; recovery is pending official vendor update or formal remediation guidance from Endpoint Engineering.

title: Clear the browser cache
product: Web browsers (Chrome reported in the call; exact browser steps were not documented)
symptoms: A user asks how to clear a browser’s cached data. The ticket description says the browser was not identified, but the call transcript records Chrome. The technician’s instructions were generic rather than browser-specific.
steps: Confirm which browser the user is using; the call in this incident identified Chrome.
In the browser’s Settings, select the option to clear the cache. The incident does not document the exact menu path or other options to select.

If the cache-clearing option is not apparent, or the user needs browser-specific guidance, consult the approved instructions for that browser or escalate to the service desk. The recorded guidance does not establish steps beyond Settings > clear cache.
resolution: The ticket records that the customer was able to clear the browser cache after receiving instructions. The transcript does not confirm completion, and the exact Chrome steps were not recorded; treat the outcome as reported in the ticket, not as a verified browser-specific procedure.
